note: Abilene on I-20 with Abilene Regional airport and Dyess AFB; covers Sweetwater to the west and Clyde. Edges with San Angelo and Wichita Falls run through ranch land; the rest is the 100 km arc over empty plain.

p_note: 2020 census urban area Austin: 1,809,888 (US Census Bureau 2020 urban areas, via Texas Demographic Center (2020 Census Urban Areas, May 2023) and citypopulation.de); p was the city-proper figure
note: Austin with Austin-Bergstrom airport; covers Round Rock, Georgetown, Cedar Park, San Marcos and Bastrop along I-35 and US-290. Meets San Antonio between San Marcos and New Braunfels, Waco north of Georgetown and College Station east of Elgin.

p_note: p stands: 2020 urban area 146,649 (Texas Demographic Center), 1.3 times p
note: Beaumont-Port Arthur on the Neches with Jack Brooks airport; covers Port Arthur, Nederland, Orange and Vidor. The Sabine River state line is not the edge: Lake Charles, (LA), US meets it a few km inside Louisiana. Houston meets it west of Winnie.

p_note: 2020 census urban area College Station--Bryan: 206,137 (US Census Bureau 2020 urban areas, via Texas Demographic Center (2020 Census Urban Areas, May 2023) and citypopulation.de); p was the city-proper figure
note: College Station and Bryan with Texas A&M and Easterwood airport; covers Navasota, Brenham, Huntsville, Madisonville and Caldwell. Drawn on 2026-10-14 from edge land of Houston, Austin and Waco.

note: Corpus Christi with its international airport; covers Portland, Rockport, Port Aransas and Mustang Island, Robstown, Alice and Kingsville. Holds the bay and the near-shore Padre Island; Victoria meets it north of Rockport, McAllen across the Kenedy County ranches.

p_note: p stands: hand-set value 6,397,000 stands (RULINGS.md); the 2020 urban area is about 5.7 million
note: Hand-painted metroplex of Dallas and Fort Worth with DFW and Love Field airports; covers Denton, McKinney, Sherman, Arlington, Weatherford, Cleburne, Waxahachie and Corsicana. Tyler meets it east of Terrell, Waco north of Hillsboro.

p_note: 2020 census urban area Houston: 5,853,575 (US Census Bureau 2020 urban areas, via Texas Demographic Center (2020 Census Urban Areas, May 2023) and citypopulation.de); p was the city-proper figure
note: Houston with Bush Intercontinental and Hobby; covers The Woodlands, Conroe, Katy, Sugar Land, Pearland, Baytown and Galveston Island. The coast and Galveston Bay bound the south-east; College Station takes the land north-west of Hempstead.

note: Laredo with its international airport and the main US/Mexico truck crossings; covers Zapata and Hebbronville. The Rio Grande is a hard border with Nuevo Laredo, MX; the rest is ranch land to the 100 km arc.

p_note: 2020 census urban area McAllen (Edinburg, Mission, Pharr, Weslaco; Brownsville is a separate urban area): 779,553 (US Census Bureau 2020 urban areas, via Texas Demographic Center (2020 Census Urban Areas, May 2023) and citypopulation.de); p was the city-proper figure
note: McAllen for the lower Rio Grande Valley: Edinburg, Mission, Pharr, Harlingen and Brownsville, with McAllen, Harlingen and Brownsville airports. The Rio Grande is a hard border with Reynosa and Matamoros, MX. South Padre Island is left out on purpose (Colin, 2026-10-14: materially distinct despite the causeway).

p_note: p stands: 2020 urban area about 1,992,689, 1.3 times p
note: San Antonio with its international airport and Joint Base San Antonio; covers New Braunfels, Seguin, Boerne, Kerrville and Pleasanton. Austin meets it between New Braunfels and San Marcos; Victoria east of Karnes City.

p_note: 2020 census urban area Texarkana TX--AR: 78,744 (US Census Bureau 2020 urban areas, via Texas Demographic Center (2020 Census Urban Areas, May 2023) and citypopulation.de); p was the city-proper figure
note: Texarkana spans the Texas/Arkansas line, with Texarkana Regional airport; covers Hope, De Queen, Atlanta and Mount Pleasant along I-30. Shreveport, Hot Springs and Tyler meet it; the state line is no barrier.

note: Tyler with Tyler Pounds airport; covers Longview (East Texas Regional airport), Kilgore, Jacksonville, Athens and Palestine. Shreveport, (LA), US holds Marshall to the east; Dallas-Fort Worth meets it east of Terrell.

note: Eagle Pass on the Rio Grande opposite Piedras Negras, MX (hard border); covers Eidson Road, Uvalde, Crystal City and Carrizo Springs. Del Rio and Laredo meet it over empty brush country.

note: Midland with Midland International airport, shared with Odessa 30 km west; covers Big Spring, Andrews, Stanton and Lamesa. The Odessa edge runs north-west between the two cities; Permian Basin oil field land on all sides.

note: Odessa, 30 km west of Midland and sharing its airport; covers West Odessa, Monahans, Kermit and Crane. Pecos lies beyond 100 km and is in no city.

note: San Angelo with Goodfellow AFB and Mathis Field; covers Ballinger, Eden and Eldorado. Abilene and Midland meet it to the north; the rest is the 100 km arc over the Edwards Plateau ranch land.
